design.fdr_method: BH across all 36 taxon-level association p values
design.statistic: RV unsigned, signed Pearson for independently scalar constructs; matched all nine constructs on identical observations/taxa

observed_summary.interpretation: Association more exceptional than independent shuffling of observed taxon labels, not a phylogenetic random-evolution or adaptive selection test.

target_pairs.interpretation: Photo presentation axis vs head elongation coupled at taxon scale; biomechanical and camera-pose hypotheses both remain; no head-centred direct angle measurement.
More saturated visible corolla colour co-occurs with greater 2D involucral outline projections; not anatomical thorns, protective effect, or herbivore–pollinator compensatory adaptation.
No detectable pooled association; this cannot establish trait independence, functional substitution or lack of correlational selection.
At observation-within-taxon scale, two image-silhouette measurements from the same involucral contour are more integrated than across taxon medians; may reflect common measurement, not function.
Heterogeneous 3D image ratios do not support significant head-orientation/involucre integration under taxon shuffled null.

exploratory_grafted_phylogeny_sensitivit.meaning: 52 alternative trees include 50 randomized grafts; NOT 52 independent evolved Cirsium phylogenies; 17/42 focal taxa are direct children of a large polytomy in scenario 1/3.
exploratory_grafted_phylogeny_sensitivit.methods: Experimental secondary sensitivity: GLS Brownian covariance from rooted mega-tree, fixed lambda 1 versus per-pair ML lambda, with/without six covariates. Not a primary valid within-genus reconstructed genealogy; phylogenetic P not proof of selection.
exploratory_grafted_phylogeny_sensitivit.decision: The apparent orientation×projection significance under enforced lambda=1 reverses under lambda optimized from data; do not promote this as phylogenetic coupling. Other two pairs are model-consistent but tree grafting and trait sampling prevent correlated-evolution inference.

biological_function_models.test: if real spine length, armature and calibrated floral visible/UV signal jointly increase legitimate pollen contact while decreasing external herbivore successful oviposition without excluding parasitoids, potential complementary guild-selective trait association
biological_function_models.rivals: pigment chemistry/UV/heat; camera colour balance; shared ancestry/ecology; projected roughness not spine

biological_function_models.test: orientation×head shape modifies rain-wetting and diurnal effective pollen contact and enemy approach geometry on same head
biological_function_models.rivals: camera pose, flower phenophase, geography, mechanical head angle

biological_function_models.test: trait effect interaction on guild-specific routes can be strong despite weak marginal trait covariance; fitness cross-over between guild regimes required
biological_function_models.rivals: no direct interaction or shared development; null observed correlation isn't proof of compensation

scope_limits: Only head photo phenotypes, not explicit floral fitness or true spine force; GloBI has no validated same-head guild or effective pollen/seed fate in this cohort.
Taxon shuffling ignores shared evolutionary history and origin replication.
Signed correlations and partials reflect observational associations; photo/camera artefacts remain.
Among-taxon RV is not coevolutionary rate or phylogenetic transition overlap.
No user field/collection permission implied and no new biology confirmed by mechanistic simulation.
